==English== {{wikipedia|+ (grip),+ (mathematics),+ (computing)}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈhæn.d(ə)l/}} ** {{audio|en|EN-AU ck1 handle.ogg|a=AU}} *** {{IPA|en|[ˈheə̯n.d(ə)ɫ]|[ˈhɛə̯n.d(ə)ɫ]|a=æ-raising}} **** {{audio|en|en-us-handle.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|ændəl|s=2}} * {{hyph|en|han|dle}} ===Etymology 1=== From {{der|en|enm|handel}}, {{m|enm|handle}}, from {{der|en|ang|handle||handle}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*handulā||handle}}. See verb below. Cognate with {{cog|de|Hantel||dumbbell, barbell}}, {{cog|da|handel||handle}}. Related to {{m|en|hand}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # The part of an object which is (designed to be) held in the hand when used or moved. # An [[instrument]] for effecting a purpose (either literally or figuratively); a [[tool]], or an [[opportunity]] or [[pretext]]. #* {{RQ:South Twelve Sermons|passage=They overturned him to all his interests by the sure but fatal '''handle''' of his own good nature.}} # {{lb|en|gambling}} The [[gross]] amount of [[wagering]] within a given period of time or for a given event at one of more establishments. #: {{ux|en|The daily '''handle''' of a Las Vegas casino is typically millions of dollars.}} #* {{quote-book |en |title=Gambling in America: an encyclopedia of history, issues, and society |page=421 |author=William Norman Thompson |year=2001 |isbn=9781576071595 |url=http://books.google.com/books?id=-9eNVovFFMoC |passage=For a casino table game,the handle is difficult to determine, as it consists of all the bets made in every game, whether by chip or by cash play.}} #* {{quote-book |en |title=The economics of casino gambling |page=77 |author=Douglas M. Walker |year=2007 |isbn=9783540351023 |url=http://books.google.com/books?id=MiO7kYe8ztUC |passage=The results for the dog racing model indicate that increases in lottery sales and decreases in horse racing '''handle''' and casino revenues in the state in question statistically increase dog racing '''handle'''.}} # {{lb|en|textiles}} The tactile qualities of a fabric, e.g., softness, firmness, elasticity, fineness, resilience, and other qualities perceived by touch. # {{lb|en|slang}} A [[name]] or [[nickname]], especially as an [[identifier]] over the [[radio]] or [[Internet]]. #: {{cot|en|alias|call sign|pseudonym}} #* {{quote-book |en |title=A 4th course of chicken soup for the soul |year=1997 |page=312 |author=Jack Canfield; Hanoch McCarty |isbn=9781558744592 |url=http://books.google.com/books?id=Um3-9MdLr_0C |passage=We sat together at the restaurant and asked him about his '''handle''' (CB name).}} # {{lb|en|slang}} A [[title]] attached to one's name, such as ''Doctor'' or ''Colonel''. #: {{ux|en|The successful businessman was knighted and acquired a '''handle''' to his name.}} # {{lb|en|computing}} A [[reference]] to an object or structure that can be stored in a [[variable]]. #: {{ux|en|This article describes how to find the module name from the window '''handle'''.}} #* {{quote-book |en |title=MATLAB programming for engineers |page=354 |author=Stephen J. Chapman |year=2008 |isbn=9780495244493 |url=http://books.google.com/books?id=fhpotPvv7v8C |passage=By contrast, when a host function creates a handle for a nested function and returns that '''handle''' to a calling program, the host function's workspace is created and ''remains in existence for as long as the function handle remains in existence.''}} # {{lb|en|UK|informal}} A traditional [[dimpled]] [[glass]] with a handle, for serving a [[pint]] of [[beer]]. #: {{syn|en|jug}} # {{lb|en|Australia|chiefly|_|Northern Territory|New Zealand}} A 10 fluid ounce (285 mL) glass of beer. # {{lb|en|US}} A half-gallon (1.75-liter) bottle of alcohol. #* {{quote-book |en |year=2014 |author=Ray Stoeser; Josh Cuffe |title=Bury My Body Down By the Highway Side |page=83 |passage=Josh bought a fifth of Evan Williams for Andrew as a token of gratitude and Ray, because of the financial constraints, purchased the cheapest '''handle''' of whiskey he could find: Heaven Hill.}} # {{lb|en|geography|Newfoundland|and|Labrador|rare}} A [[point]], an extremity of land. #: {{ux|en|the '''Handle''' of the Sug in Newfoundland}} # {{lb|en|topology}} A [[topological space]] [[homeomorphic]] to a [[ball]] but viewed as a [[product]] of two lower[[-dimensional]] balls. # {{lb|en|algebraic geometry}} The [[smooth]], [[irreducible]] [[subcurve]] of a [[comb]] which connects to each of the other [[component]]s in exactly one point. # {{lb|en|slang}} A person's [[nose]]. #* {{quote-book |en |year=1811 |author=Charles Lamb |title=Prince Dorus |passage=That Nose, which in the infant could annoy, / Was grown a perfect nuisance in the boy. / Whene'er he walk'd, his '''Handle''' went before, / Long as the snout of Ferret, or Wild Boar; {{...}}}} # {{lb|en|horse racing|gambling}} The amount wagered in the various [[pari-mutuel]] [[pool]]s for a particular event or events. =====Synonyms===== * {{sense|285 mL glass of beer}} {{l|en|pot}} Cognate with {{cog|fy|handelje}}, {{m|fy|hanneljen}}, {{m|fy|hanljen|t=to handle, treat}}, {{cog|nl|handelen|t=to handle, deal, act, negotiate}}, {{cog|de|handeln|t=to act, trade, negotiate, behave}}, {{cog|sv|handla|t=to buy, trade, deal}}, {{cog|is|höndla|t=to handle}}. ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To touch; to feel or hold with the hand(s). #* {{RQ:Spenser Amoretti|sonnet=1 |passage=Happy, ye leaves! when as those lilly hands [...] Shall '''handle''' you.}} #* {{RQ:KJV|Luke|24|39|passage='''Handle''' me, and see; for a spirit hath not flesh.}} #* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Regained|book=1|passage=[...] about his altar, '''handling''' holy things}} # {{lb|en|transitive|rare}} To accustom to the hand; to take care of with the hands. #* {{quote-book |en |year=1679 |author={{w |Sir William Temple, 1st Baronet |William Temple}}|title=An essay upon the advancement of trade in Ireland. |passage=The hardness of the winters forces the breeders to house and '''handle''' their colts for at least six months every year.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To manage, use, or [[wield]] with the hands. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare King Lear|4|6|passage=That fellow '''handles''' his bow like a crowkeeper}} #* {{quote-book |en |year=1976 |author=Mel Hallin Bolster |title=Crazy Snake and the Smoked Meat Rebellion |page=66 |passage=Light on his feet for a big man, he '''handled''' the rifle like a pistol.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To manage, control, or direct. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Measure|5|1|passage=You shall see how I'll '''handle''' her}} #* {{RQ:Guardian |date=December 16, 2011 |author=Denis Campbell |title=Hospital staff 'lack skills to cope with dementia patients' |url=http://www.guardian.co.uk/society/2011/dec/16/hospital-staff-dementia-patients |passage=The findings emerged from questionnaires filled in by 2,211 staff in 145 wards of 55 hospitals in England and Wales and 105 observations of care of dementia patients. Two-thirds of staff said they had not had enough training to provide proper care, 50% said they had not been trained how to communicate properly with such patients and 54% had not been told how to '''handle''' challenging or aggressive behaviour.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261013072428/https://www.theguardian.com/society/2011/dec/16/hospital-staff-dementia-patients|archivedate=13 October 2026}} #* {{quote-book |en |year=2015 |author=Nora Quick |title=Case of the Missing Millionaire |passage=“You also '''handle''' the accounts for Julie Wojakowski, what about her? Any recent deposits in that amount?”}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To treat, to deal with (in a specified way). #: {{ux|en|she '''handled''' the news with grace}} #: {{ux|en|the Persians '''handled''' the French ambassador shamefully}} #* {{RQ:Marlowe Tamburlaine|part=1|scene=iii|page=50|passage=I will not tell thee how Ile '''handle''' thee,
But euery common ſouldier of my Camp
Shall ſmile to see thy miſerable ſtate.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 6-2|1|4|passage=How wert thou '''handled''' being prisoner?}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To deal with (a subject, argument, topic, or theme) in speaking, in writing, or in art. #* {{RQ:Bacon Essayes|chapter=Of Envy|passage=We will '''handle''' what persons are apt to envy others...}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To receive and transfer; to have pass through one's hands; hence, to buy and sell. #: {{ux|en|a merchant '''handles''' a variety of goods, or a large stock}} # {{lb|en|transitive|rare}} To be concerned with; to be an expert in. #* {{RQ:KJV|Jeremiah|2|8||They that '''handle''' the law knew me not}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[put up with]]; to endure (and continue to function). #: {{ux|en|I can't '''handle''' this hot weather.}} #* {{quote-book |en |year=2014 |author=Andrew Stellman; Jennifer Greene |title=Learning Agile: Understanding Scrum, XP, Lean, and Kanban |isbn=1449363857 |passage=For example, a program that loads data from a file needs to '''handle''' the case where that file is not found.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To use the hands. #* {{RQ:KJV|Psalms|115|7|passage=They [idols made of gold and silver] have hands, but they '''handle''' not}} # {{lb|en|soccer|intransitive}} To illegally touch the ball with the hand or arm; to commit [[handball]]. # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[behave]] in a particular way when handled (managed, controlled, directed). #: {{syn|en|ride}} #: {{ux|en|the car '''handles''' well}} =====Synonyms===== {{checksense|en}} {{col|en |feel |finger |touch |deal |manage |treat }} =====Derived terms===== {{col|en|behandle |handleability |handled the ball |handle oneself |handlesome |handle up |handle with kid gloves |handle without gloves |handle without mittens |Jesus handle |manhandle |mishandle |outhandle |overhandle |rehandle |too hot to handle |well-handled }} =====Related terms===== * {{l|en|hand}} =====Descendants===== * {{desc|nl|bor=1|handelen}} * {{desc|de|bor=1|händeln|handeln}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top|to touch;
